title: GEOM-Drugs Revisited: Toward More Chemically Accurate Benchmarks for 3D Molecule Generation
experiments_summary: The study performed the following experiments and applied the following methods: (1) Re-evaluation of molecular stability metrics: Five models (EQGAT-Diff, Megalodon-quick, SemlaFlow, FlowMol2, Megalodon-flow) were re-evaluated using 5,000 generated molecules per model under multiple valency computation schemes: the original (buggy) implementation, a corrected 1.5 aromatic bond contribution, and a refined aromaticity-dependent lookup table indexed by (element, number of aromatic bonds, formal charge, non-aromatic valency). (2) Dataset curation: The raw GEOM-Drugs dataset was filtered to remove molecules fragmented due to failed GFN2-xTB geometry optimization (0.18% of data excluded), and a fully Kekulized version of the dataset was prepared by converting all aromatic bonds to alternating single and double bonds. (3) Retraining of generative models: The same five models were retrained on the reprocessed Kekulized GEOM-Drugs dataset, and molecular stability and connected validity (V&C) were recomputed under the corrected evaluation protocol. (4) GFN2-xTB-based geometric evaluation: For each of the five models and a 5,000-molecule baseline subset from GEOM-Drugs, generated structures were subjected to GFN2-xTB geometry optimization. Metrics computed included median and mean relaxation energy (delta E_relax), average bond length differences, average bond angle differences, and average torsion angle differences between generated and GFN2-xTB-optimized structures. Confidence intervals were computed by splitting each set of 5,000 molecules into five equal splits of 1,000 molecules each. (5) MMFF vs. GFN2-xTB comparison: MMFF-optimized structures were re-optimized with GFN2-xTB, and the resulting geometric and energetic discrepancies were quantified using the same structural displacement metrics to benchmark the adequacy of MMFF as an evaluation reference for GEOM-Drugs.
